findings.summary: Verisum reduces the hallucination rate on Tamsin-News to 8.7%, compared to 11.0% for Corran-Sum with salience pre-filtering and 15.1% for Corran-Sum alone.
findings.scope: Tamsin-News test split (3,000 articles), hallucination rate metric
findings.caveats: Single training run; no statistical tests reported.

findings.summary: The reduction from Corran-Sum to Verisum (15.1% to 8.7%, a 42% relative decrease) is larger than the reduction from Corran-Sum to Corran-Sum + salience filter (15.1% to 11.0%, a 27% relative decrease) in this evaluation.
findings.caveats: No statistical test; single run; comparison is within this dataset only.

findings.summary: The 27% relative reduction from salience pre-filtering in this study is similar to the 31% average reduction reported by Varga & Sandoval (2021), though the absolute rates differ (11.0% vs 9.8% on average).
findings.scope: Tamsin-News test split vs three news benchmarks in P1
findings.caveats: Different datasets and implementations; no statistical comparison.

findings.summary: ROUGE-L for Verisum (38.9) is slightly higher than for Corran-Sum (38.2) and Corran-Sum + salience filter (38.0), but differences are small and no significance test is reported.
